segments.he: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: הַבוּ לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי לִפְלוֹנִי, וְלִנְסֵיב בְּרַתִּי. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אַרְבַּע מְאָה — שָׁקֵיל, וּבְרַתֵּיה — אִי בָּעֵי נָסֵיב, אִי בָּעֵי — לָא נָסֵיב.
segments.en: In relation to the previous case, in which one makes a conditional statement and only part of his statement is accepted, the Gemara relates a somewhat similar incident: «A certain man said to» those tending to him, in the form of a will: «Give four hundred zuz to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter. Rav Pappa said:» The «four hundred» zuz «he takes, but» as for the benefactor’s «daughter, if he wishes, he may marry» her, and «if he wishes, he» need «not marry» her.

segments.he: טַעְמָא דְּאָמַר הַבוּ לֵיהּ וְלִנְסֵיב, אֲבָל אִי אָמַר לִנְסֵיב וְהַבוּ לֵיהּ, אִי נָסֵיב — שָׁקֵיל, וְאִי לָא נָסֵיב — לָא שָׁקֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: «The reason» is solely «that he said» it in this manner: «Give him» the money «and let him marry» my daughter, mentioning the gift before the condition. «However, if» he specified the condition first, by «saying: Let him marry» my daughter «and give him» the money, in that case, «if he marries» her, «he takes» the money, but «if he does not marry» her, «he may not take» it.
